headline: Dynamite was invented to be the safe explosive
dek: Nitroglycerin was killing the people who handled it. Alfred Nobel found a fix.

slides.label: The bright idea
slides.title: Tame the oil
slides.text: Nitroglycerin was a powerful blasting oil, and it went off in transit and in storage. In 1864 an explosion at Nobel's factory in Stockholm killed five people, including his younger brother Emil. The city banned the experiments.

slides.label: It worked
slides.title: Dynamite
slides.text: Nobel soaked nitroglycerin into a porous earth called kieselguhr and patented it in 1867 as dynamite. Even soaked through, it was quite safe to handle. His Krümmel plant made 11 tons that year, 3,150 in 1874.
slides.alt: Women in aprons mixing dynamite in wooden boxes along a bench, with a man standing at the left, inside a timber factory shed
slides.credit: Mixing dynamite at Nobel's Ardeer factory, Scotland, 1897. Scott Photo, Ardrossan. Public domain.

slides.label: The backfire
slides.title: Easy to carry, for anyone
slides.text: A stable explosive can be carried into a city and left behind. From 1881 to 1885 Irish republican bombers waged a dynamite campaign in Britain, hitting the House of Commons and the Tower of London in 1885.
also: Source: Niall Whelehan, The Dynamiters, Cambridge University Press
slides.alt: Engraving of a bomb going off in Westminster Hall, throwing back the people nearby, under two smaller scenes of shattered stonework and the wrecked House of Commons
slides.credit: The dynamite explosions at the Houses of Parliament, The Graphic, 1885. Henry William Brewer. Public domain.

slides.label: What came next
slides.title: Powder for armies
slides.text: In 1887 Nobel patented ballistite, a nearly smokeless powder for firing military projectiles, and Italy's army adopted it. In 1894 he bought the Bofors ironworks in Sweden, the basis of the Bofors arms company.
slides.alt: A paper rocket case with a wooden nose and metal fittings, inscribed in ink and dated September 1896, in a museum display
slides.credit: Ballistite rocket case by Alfred Nobel and W. T. Unge, 1896, Tekniska museet. Photo: Daderot. CC0.

slides.label: Could anyone have seen it coming?
slides.title: Yes, in his lifetime
slides.text: Armies used dynamite in the Franco-Prussian War of 1870 to 1871, three years after the patent. Bombers used it in Britain from 1881, and in 1887 Nobel patented a powder for armies himself. The uses for war and terror were plain in his lifetime.

slides.label: The ledger
slides.title: Worth it?
gains: One plant's dynamite output: 11 tons in 1867, 3,150 tons in 1874 (Nobel Foundation)
Lucerne to Milan by rail in about 5.5 hours instead of 27, once the Gotthard tunnel opened in 1882
A much lower risk of accidental explosion than liquid nitroglycerin
costs: A bombing campaign in Britain, 1881 to 1885, aimed at Parliament and the Tower of London
A smokeless military powder, ballistite, adopted by Italy's army
Weapons for both sides of the Franco-Prussian War, 1870 to 1871, within three years of the patent
slides.text: Dynamite built tunnels, mines and roads. It also put a portable bomb within reach of anyone who could buy it.

slides.label: Credit for trying
slides.title: We owe him one
slides.text: Nobel took on a deadly problem: a blasting oil that exploded in factories, in storage and in transit. He made it safe to handle. In 1895 his will left most of his fortune to prizes for those who confer the greatest benefit on mankind.

slides.label: How the pattern works
slides.title: From accident to intent
slides.text: The danger of nitroglycerin was that it went off when nobody meant it to. Dynamite fixed that. The same stability made it easy to carry, hide and set off on purpose. The risk moved from the factory floor to whoever held the stick.

slides.label: How you do this
slides.title: Your fixes move risk too
slides.text: Analysts kept breaking the fragile scripts that pulled customer data, so you build a one-click export. The broken scripts stop. Now anyone can put the whole customer list on a laptop. The risk didn't go away. It moved.
also: A public-link setting that ends the sharing requests
A shared password that ends the access requests

slides.label: Lessons
slides.title: What we take from it
items: Making something safe to handle also makes it easy to use, by anyone.
A fix aimed at accidents does nothing about intent.
The people who use an invention decide much of what it does.
